We (the wife and I) make a lot of different kinds of sausage. Italian,Ukrainian,Polish just to name a few styles. Last batch we did was Italian hot links. I would be hard pressed to name my favorite one but the smoked garlic is my favorite compared to with the BBQ one. Cheers!
Do you need a lot of equipment to get started beyond a meat grinder, filler nozzle, and casings? Do you find it difficult to get the balance of meat and fat and spices right?

Well I couldn't find the episode I was thinking of, but, the show is called Food Jammers. They did a great episode where they fermented their own cold cuts and cheese at home. IIRC they wanted to make a sandwich from scratch, your google fu is probably better then mine.

At any rate, it`s very easy to start making sausage! Get some ground meat and try a couple recipe mixes you find online. Make sausage patties first, then if you like doing it grab one of THESE and some natural casings and you're well on your way!

I wouldn't consider posting a different sub shilling, so no worries. Basically there are two methods of preserving sausage. The first is to smoke the second is to ferment. Fermented sausage is what is commonly known as cold cuts. There is no heat in the process and the sausage is left in a controlled environment (temp and humidity) to cure by fermentation.
